rubric.why: Identifies the required form of the coefficient.
rubric.description: The number is written as a coefficient from 1 up to, but not including, 10.
rubric.how: Award for stating the coefficient range.

rubric.why: Scientific notation uses a power of ten to represent place value.
rubric.description: The coefficient is multiplied by an integral power of 10.
rubric.how: Award for specifying multiplication by a power of ten.

modelAnswer: Scientific notation is a way of writing a number as the product of a number between 1 and 10 and an integral power of 10.

items.followUp: When is the zero error of a screw gauge positive?

rubric.why: Locates the circular-scale zero when the screw gauge is closed.
rubric.description: With the jaws closed, the zero of the circular scale is above the reference line.
rubric.how: Award for correctly identifying the zero's position.

rubric.why: Specifies the condition under which zero error is observed.
rubric.description: The position is observed when the screw gauge jaws are fully closed.
rubric.how: Award for stating the closed-jaw condition.

modelAnswer: When the jaws of a screw gauge are closed, its zero error is negative if the zero of the circular scale lies above the reference line.

items.followUp: What is meant by a derived quantity? Give one example.

rubric.why: Shows that basic quantities are not derived from other quantities.
rubric.description: Basic quantities are independent of other quantities.

rubric.why: Identifies basic quantities as measurable quantities.
rubric.description: They are physical quantities that are not defined in terms of other quantities.
rubric.how: Award for describing them as physical quantities.

modelAnswer: Basic quantities are physical quantities that are independent of other quantities.

items.followUp: What does the slope of a distance-time graph represent?

rubric.why: Identifies the form in which a graph presents information.
rubric.description: A graph is a visual or graphical representation.
rubric.how: Award for describing a graph as a visual representation.

rubric.description: It shows the relationship between two quantities (variables).
rubric.how: Award for identifying the relationship between two quantities.

modelAnswer: A graph is a visual representation of the relationship between two quantities.

rubric.why: Gives the defining basis of distance.
rubric.description: Distance is the total length of the path travelled and has magnitude only.
rubric.how: Award for identifying distance as total path length.

rubric.why: Gives the defining basis of displacement and distinguishes it from distance.
rubric.description: Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from initial to final position, in a specified direction.
rubric.how: Award for identifying displacement as directed straight-line change in position.

modelAnswer: Distance is the total length of the path travelled and has magnitude only.
Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the initial to the final position in a specified direction.

rubric.why: Distinguishes positive acceleration by its effect on velocity or speed.
rubric.description: Positive acceleration increases the velocity (or speed) of a body.
rubric.how: Award for linking positive acceleration to an increase.

rubric.why: Distinguishes negative acceleration by its effect on velocity or speed.
rubric.description: Negative acceleration decreases the velocity (or speed) of a body; it is also called retardation.
rubric.how: Award for linking negative acceleration to a decrease.

modelAnswer: Positive acceleration increases the velocity of a body with time.
Negative acceleration decreases the velocity of a body with time and is also called retardation.

items.followUp: What is the difference between mass and weight?

rubric.why: Defines mass in terms of the matter in a body.
rubric.description: Mass is the quantity or amount of matter in a body.
rubric.how: Award for defining mass as the amount of matter.

rubric.why: Defines weight as a force due to gravity.
rubric.description: Weight is the gravitational force acting on a body.
rubric.how: Award for defining weight as the force of gravity on a body.

modelAnswer: Mass is the quantity of matter in a body.
Weight is the gravitational force acting on a body.

items.followUp: State two useful effects of friction.

rubric.why: Identifies damage caused by friction between surfaces.
rubric.description: Friction causes wear and tear of moving parts or surfaces.
rubric.how: Award for stating that friction wears surfaces or moving parts.

rubric.why: Identifies energy loss caused by friction.
rubric.how: Award for stating that friction generates heat or wastes energy.

modelAnswer: Friction causes wear and tear of moving parts and surfaces.
Friction produces heat, resulting in a loss of useful energy.
